name: Toni Basil
hook: A choreographer who brought street dance to television and made 'Mickey', a cheerleader chant that Weird Al turned into an 'I Love Lucy' tribute.
blurb: Toni Basil was born Antonia Basilotta in Philadelphia in 1943 and grew up in Las Vegas. She was a dancer and choreographer long before she was a pop star. She was an assistant choreographer on the 'T.A.M.I. Show' (1964), helped start and managed The Lockers, a group that brought street dance to television, choreographed David Bowie's Diamond Dogs (1974) and Glass Spider (1987) tours, and co-directed Talking Heads' 'Once in a Lifetime' video (1981). Her 1982 hit 'Mickey', a cover of Racey's 'Kitty' (1979), from her album 'Word of Mouth' on Chrysalis, went to number one in America in December 1982. She came up with, directed and choreographed the video herself, dancing in her old high-school cheerleader uniform. At 75 she choreographed the film 'Once Upon a Time in Hollywood' (2019).
